title: Grateful Dead Live at Paramount Theatre on 1972-07-26
lineage: MR > PCM > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of a mellow mid‑'70s show, highlighted by an incredible Dark Star → Comes A Time sequence and crisp renditions of China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean soundboard source that most listeners describe as crystal‑clear and enjoyable despite its age. Musically the concert is relaxed yet inspired, with Dark Star flowing seamlessly into Comes A Time, plus standout moments like China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider and He's Gone. Overall the performance feels warm and engaging, making it a favorite for fans who love the mellow side of the 1972 era.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews (17 out of 21) award five stars and praise both the performance and the sound quality; only one low‑rating review is present, yielding an average of ~4.6 stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Most reviewers call the audio crisp, awesome and excellent; a few note minor issues such as missing part of "Casey Jones" or slightly uneven harmonies, but overall the sound is clear and well‑balanced for a 1972 source.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical mid‑72 setlist that stays relaxed and laid‑back; strong opening trio, smooth transition into a mellow second set with memorable banter.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his incredible voice and guitar tone – described as "slices of velvet moonbeam" and "sooooooo incredible."
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for delivering huge bass bombs, especially during the Dark Star jam.
band_member_comments.Bob: His rhythm driving the band is highlighted as "fantastic rhythm driving the train."
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith (keys) stands out in pre‑verse jams; keyboards are described as delightful and a key part of the jazzy vibe.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann called a "machine" with thunderous space melt‑down moments; overall drumming praised for power.
